status_summary: Several parts are operative, one is blocked in court, and the anti-fraud item is unverified. In 2025 the Attorney General overruled two Garland-era decisions: Matter of S-S-F-M- (decided 2025-09-02) overruled the 2021 Matter of A-B- III, and EOIR's decision index also lists Matter of R-E-R-M- & J-D-R-M- (A.G. 2025) overruling the 2021 Matter of L-E-A-; no review of every Garland-era decision was found. Two rules revive 2020 rules: a DHS and DOJ rule of 2025-12-30 confirmed the 2025-12-31 effective date of the December 2020 Security Bars and Processing rule with a partial withdrawal, and the Board of Immigration Appeals appellate-procedures interim final rule of 2026-02-06 adopts measures from the 2020 appellate rule; on 2026-03-08 the U.S. District Court for the District of Columbia set aside the substantive parts of that interim rule (per a court-docket summary) and the case is stayed pending a final rule. EOIR statistics generated 2026-07-24 show pending cases at 3,469,569 at the end of the third quarter of fiscal 2026, down from 3,722,776 at the end of fiscal 2025, with 662 immigration judges on board against 735 at the end of fiscal 2024; EOIR announced 47 more judges sworn in on 2026-09-24. DOJ moved to terminate the Flores settlement on 2025-05-22 and the district court denied the motion on 2025-08-15. The Civil Rights Division's Immigrant and Employee Rights Section lists employer settlements from 2025-09-29 through 2026-08-04 and a suit filed 2026-04-28 over excluding U.S. workers. The government's appeal of the denial (Flores v. Blanche, Ninth Circuit No. 25-6308) was calendared for argument on 2026-06-02; no decision was found through 2026-10-13.

timeline.event: A federal district judge in Los Angeles denies the Justice Department's motion (filed 2025-05-22) to terminate the Flores settlement, calling it a repeat of the 2019 attempt.

The Attorney General issues Matter of S-S-F-M- (29 I&N Dec. 206 and 207), overruling Matter of A-B- III (2021); the EOIR decisions index for volume 29 also lists Matter of R-E-R-M- & J-D-R-M- (A.G. 2025), overruling Matter of L-E-A- (2021).
DHS and EOIR publish a final rule confirming the 2025-12-31 effective date of the December 2020 Security Bars and Processing rule and withdrawing parts of it that conflict with later rules.

EOIR publishes an interim final rule making Board of Immigration Appeals merits review discretionary, shortening most appeal deadlines to 10 days and adopting briefing measures from the 2020 appellate rule (effective 2026-03-09).

In Amica Center for Immigrant Rights v. EOIR (D.D.C., No. 1:26-cv-00696), the court sets aside the substantive parts of the appellate interim final rule and remands; on 2026-04-10 the case is stayed pending a final rule (per a court-docket summary).

The Ninth Circuit calendar lists Flores v. Blanche, No. 25-6308, for argument on 2026-06-02 in Seattle (15 minutes per side): the government's appeal of the district court order denying its motion to terminate the 1997 Flores settlement agreement (district docket 2:85-cv-04544-DMG-AGR).
EOIR statistics generated this day show 3,469,569 pending cases at the end of the third quarter of fiscal 2026 and 662 immigration judges on board (53 temporary judges as of 2026-06-30).
EOIR proposes a rule defining immigration judges' contempt authority and setting a civil money penalty process for contempt.
EOIR announces the swearing-in of 47 immigration judges and 6 temporary immigration judges, appointed by Todd Blanche.

uncertainties: The 2025 Attorney General decisions are dated from the S-S-F-M- document (2025-09-02); the volume 29 index gives only the year for R-E-R-M- and Negusie, so those dates and the Negusie holding (it vacates a stay and restores a 2020 decision) were not independently confirmed. The 2026-03-08 ruling is taken from a Civil Rights Litigation Clearinghouse summary, not the court opinion, and that page also labels the relief a preliminary injunction while the docket describes partial summary judgment; whether the government appealed was not checked. The Flores denial comes from a wire report republished on a local site; whether the government appealed to the Ninth Circuit was not found (a search surfaced only older Flores coverage). The EOIR policy memoranda list and the Attorney General decisions list for 2026 could not be retrieved (pages returned errors), so rescissions of Biden-era policy memos beyond EOIR's 2025-09-04 statement were not re-verified, and anti-fraud steps, immigration judge removals and appointee placement were not found. IJ headcount comes from an EOIR hiring table that does not show separations. Searches run: Matter of S-S-F-M- and R-E-R-M- decision dates; Flores motion outcome (two searches); lawsuits against the BIA interim final rule. Ninth Circuit No. 25-6308: the calendar page was read, but the appellate docket itself was not retrieved and no decision was found in searches through 2026-10-13. Meese, opened 2026-07-20), was stayed on 2026-08-13 pending No. 25-6308 per a Justia docket page last retrieved 2026-08-13; its subject was not identified.
